target.access: Herdr 0.7.3 with SSH panes targeting one remote macOS worker

checks.contract_clause: One human-visible Herdr pane can host and control one remote AGY process without tmux
checks.evidence: The Herdr pane had SSH as its foreground controller-side process, displayed the native AGY TUI, accepted two distinct prompts, and returned two exact distinct tokens. The remote worker had one matching AGY process and no tmux server.

checks.contract_clause: Three uniquely labeled Herdr tabs can run and control three AGY processes concurrently
checks.evidence: Three unique tabs mapped to three distinct panes and three remote AGY processes. Three unique prompts were dispatched concurrently and each pane returned its matching exact token.

checks.contract_clause: The workflow persists across human client detach and reattach
checks.evidence: The Herdr server remained running, but the active human client was not detached during this proof.

checks.contract_clause: The primitive is qualified for Puppet ordinary operation
checks.evidence: The proof reused a pre-existing operator Herdr session and used bounded terminal reads. Puppet ordinary operation requires controller-owned identity and transcript-blind lifecycle evidence.

anti_cheat_probes.probe: Changed the expected response token in the same pane
anti_cheat_probes.result: The AGY response changed to the second exact token
Each of the three panes returned only its matching token

anti_cheat_probes.probe: Rechecked remote process and tmux inventory after responses
anti_cheat_probes.result: The same three AGY process identities remained and no tmux server existed
